guard: the reaper kills a smoke broker only when its recorded owner is dead, and leaves every other broker alone
why: THE FIRST MUTATION IS THE ONE THIS FILE EXISTS FOR. An earlier version of this reaper matched the
token alone, and a tokened broker is not a leaked broker: the token records which suite minted the
tree, not that the suite is done with it. Two lanes run smokes on a shared box constantly, and the
prefix-only version was REPRODUCED listing a live lane's broker for the kill. It would have
SIGKILLed a running broker mid-suite and reddened that lane with a diagnosis pointing at its own
code. The untokened negative control could never have caught that, because the victim is tokened.
So the owner-liveness check is the load-bearing guard here, and disabling it must redden the
owner-alive control specifically.
A MUTATION CAN BE DANGEROUS TO RUN, WHICH IS ITSELF PART OF THE DESIGN. mutation-proof executes
the real suite against the real machine. The obvious mutation, deleting the prefix filter so the
reaper claims every nats-server it sees, is NOT used: measured on one box, it would kill 14
unrelated brokers rather than fail a test. Even the owner-check mutation below has a real blast
radius, since with it disabled the reaper claims any TOKENED broker regardless of owner, which is
precisely another lane's live broker. Before running this fixture, confirm no tokened broker on
the box belongs to anyone else (`reapSmokeBrokers({dryRun:true})` reporting ownedLive 0 with no
concurrent smoke run is the check). A test that damages the machine to prove a point is not a
test worth running, and that constraint shaped which mutations exist here rather than being an
excuse for having fewer.
THE SECOND MUTATION SEPARATES REPORTING FROM ACTING. The reaper both kills a process and returns a
list naming it, and a single green cell could conflate those. Removing the kill while leaving the
bookkeeping intact reddens the positive control alone and leaves 'the killed broker is named in
the report' green, which is exactly the false green this file exists to make impossible: a reaper
that reports a clean sweep it never performed.

mutations.name: the owner-liveness check is disabled, so a tokened broker is claimed while its owner is still running
mutations.find: if (alive(Number(owner[1]))) { ownedLive++; continue; } // someone is still using it
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: NEGATIVE CONTROL: a tokened broker whose owner is ALIVE is untouched
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: NEGATIVE CONTROL: a tokened broker whose owner is ALIVE is untouched

mutations.name: the reaper reports the kill without performing it
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: POSITIVE CONTROL: the broker whose owner is DEAD is killed
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: POSITIVE CONTROL: the broker whose owner is DEAD is killed
